tasks.short: Select and position microphones for recording or transmission

steps.what: Consult the actual available microphone specifications and production sound requirements
inputs: actual production sound requirements
existing available-microphone specifications
outputs: technician-read sound requirements and microphone capabilities

steps.what: Assess the actual performers, room and sound sources and determine the number, type and approximate microphone locations
inputs: technician-read sound requirements and microphone capabilities
actual room, performers, sound sources and camera constraints
outputs: technician's actual microphone selection and intended locations

steps.what: Position the selected microphones appropriately and check and refine their actual pickup
inputs: technician's actual microphone selection and intended locations
actual microphones, performers and sound
outputs: appropriately positioned microphones with checked sound pickup

tasks.design: Keep acoustic assessment and physical microphone positioning with the technician. Actual specification lookup is separate and already uses {DOCS}; no additional supported lookup or placement change is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful microphone arrangement depends on the real sound and production geometry.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing specifications support selection; no new mechanism removes physical positioning or listening.
tasks.still_hard: Room sound, performer movement and camera constraints interact.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to the actual result and choose practical placement trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: microphone selection and positioning depend on actual acoustics and production constraints, with existing specifications supporting the technician.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. Actual specification lookup is separated and fully retained; no new structured acoustic model is assumed.
The production supplies actual sound requirements and equipment specifications. Missing details are checked directly, not guessed.
This selection/positioning statement establishes no separate written report, send or system commit. No paperwork baseline is added.
All work remains, gross/net saving are zero and there is no incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual room, microphone stock and production constraints
research_questions: Does observed work reveal repeated specification lookup that an existing native view could improve?

incremental.description: No new system or placement process proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to actual specification reading, acoustic selection or physical placement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read actual playout as-run records and the station's current programming-log requirements
inputs: actual playout as-run records
station's current required log fields and exception rules
outputs: technician-read programme events and log requirements

steps.what: Reconcile actual airing observations and known deviations with the as-run events
inputs: technician-read programme events and log requirements
actual off-air observations and station personnel's deviation information
outputs: technician-checked actual programme events and exceptions

steps.what: Complete and check the actual programming log, including required timings, programme identities and known exceptions
inputs: technician-checked actual programme events and exceptions
station's current required log fields and exception rules

steps.what: Save the completed checked programming log in the station's existing log store
inputs: complete checked programming-log version

tasks.design: Configure native as-run views and draft programming-log fields in {OTHER}, the station playout/log applications. The technician reconciles actual airing and exceptions, completes all required fields and checks the exact log before saving it; a schedule alone never proves that a programme aired.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual playout events can be re-entered into a separate log view.
tasks.enabler_now: Native as-run fields can populate draft log entries where supported.
tasks.still_hard: Off-air failures, substitutions and required exceptions need actual operational evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Identify when a playout event is inconsistent with what actually aired.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for station data access and approved log configuration

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native as-run records can populate programming-log draft fields while technicians reconcile real airing and exceptions.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. Actual station/jurisdiction requirements are supplied by the station; no US requirement is presumed to apply to a European station.

OTHER means station playout and programming-log software. Existing playout supplies actual event ID, programme identity, start/end time and status; station personnel/return monitors supply actual deviation evidence.
Missing or conflicting records require manual reconciliation. No structured exception code or actual airing is inferred from the schedule.
Gross provisional saving 14.2 minus 1.5 hours of field/rule upkeep gives 12.7 net. Existing equivalent log population removes the gain.
Draft population has no hidden commit; the final save is negligible and fully retained.
unknowns: Actual required fields, native log functions and as-run completeness
research_questions: Can native draft population reduce real log entry while preserving reconciliation of off-air exceptions?

already_counted.description: Inspect events, reconcile actual airing and complete/check the log

incremental.description: Maintain log-field mappings and test station rule changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 12.7%; depends on real manual log entry beyond current native tools.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Determine the graphic's actual communication purpose, visual treatment and programme requirements
inputs: actual programme graphic request and house style
actual broadcast format and display constraints
outputs: technician's actual graphic concept and requirements

steps.what: Obtain and check the actual graphic text, names, numbers and permitted visual assets
inputs: technician's actual graphic concept and requirements
programme producer's actual text/data and permitted assets

steps.what: Produce graphics for broadcasts and check the complete asset for content, legibility, safe placement and output format
inputs: technician's actual graphic concept and requirements
technician-checked graphic content and assets
existing approved graphic templates

steps.what: Save the completed checked graphic asset in the production workspace
inputs: complete checked broadcast-graphic asset version

tasks.design: Configure native approved graphic templates in {OTHER}, the broadcast graphics application, to reuse layout and output settings. The technician chooses the visual treatment, checks actual supplied content and finishes the graphic before saving it; putting the graphic on air is a later action and is not automated here.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated layout and output setup can consume graphic-production effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native template fields can place actual text/assets within an approved layout.
tasks.still_hard: Meaning, names, numbers, visual hierarchy and on-screen legibility need human checking.
tasks.human_edge: Make the graphic communicate the right thing in the actual programme context.

ambition.what: No additional graphics volume or automatic airing assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native broadcast-graphics templates can reuse layout and output settings while technicians retain content and visual checks.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured; only repeated actual template/layout handling changes.

OTHER means broadcast graphics and asset-library applications. The programme producer supplies real names/text/data and permitted assets; the technician checks them in s2. Missing facts require clarification.
No generative visual asset, invented data feed or semantic text generation is proposed. Existing equivalent templates remove the gain.
Gross provisional saving 12.25 minus 2 hours of template/output-setting upkeep gives 10.25 net. Final save remains fully retained and earns no saving.
This task produces the asset, with no hidden on-air publish, notification or transmission action.
unknowns: Current template coverage and actual repeated layout effort
research_questions: Which real broadcast graphics still repeat layout/output setup that native templates can remove?

already_counted.description: Complete and check graphic content, placement and output format

incremental.description: Maintain approved graphic templates and test output-setting changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 10.25%; original graphic design and content checks remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe the actual filming setup, current take and technical issue needing coordination
inputs: actual filming activity and technical equipment state
actual production requirements

steps.what: Give actual technical directions to the other personnel during filming and respond to their questions and changing conditions
inputs: technician's actual filming-coordination observations
personnel's actual questions and responses
outputs: actual communicated technical directions and coordination

tasks.design: Retain live technical directions with the technician, using {OTHER}, the existing production intercom, where used. Observation and conversation are explicit; no extra report or software direction generator is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directions must respond to the actual filming conditions and personnel.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing intercom supports the conversation; no new mechanism removes the work.
tasks.still_hard: Changing takes, equipment states and crew questions require immediate contextual response.
tasks.human_edge: Choose clear, practical technical directions at the right moment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live filming directions depend on actual technical conditions and crew interaction.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. OTHER means existing production intercom; no new recording or structured cue feed is assumed.
Actual observation is separated from directions. This live-direction statement establishes no separate record write, report or send; none is invented.
No change is proposed, so gross/net saving are zero and no incremental upkeep is required.
unknowns: Actual filming format and coordination needs
research_questions: Does observed filming contain a distinct actual written cue/update task that needs separate design?

incremental.description: No new system or direction process proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to live observation or technical crew direction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

skills_to_grow: Reconcile actual airing with programming logs
Validate source fields before record saving
role.ambitious_version: Reduce actual log transcription and repeated graphics assembly while retaining acoustic placement, live directions and broadcast judgment.
